newsitem.title: USA: US lawmaker wants review of Fannie, Freddie.
newsitem.headline: US lawmaker wants review of Fannie, Freddie.

text.p: House Banking Committee chairman Jim Leach said Thursday the Clinton administration should conduct a review of the activities of Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac and the Federal Home Loan Bank System.
The Iowa Republican, a longtime critic of the government sponsored enterprises, charged the institutions were undercutting private-sector competition.

An inter-agency committee should "determine whether they are hewing to their mission or abusing governmental powers, whether they are serving the private retail sector or pre-empting it," Leach said at a hearing.
In prior months, Leach has criticized investments by Freddie Mac and a proposal by Fannie Mae to provide a form of mortgage insurance.
Rep. Richard Baker, Republican of Louisiana, said he favored creating a single federal agency with authority to oversee all three government-sponsored enterprises.

"With close to $1.7 trillion in implicit federal backing, amounting to almost 12 percent of all outstanding credit in the United States, the housing (enterprises) represent a considerable risk that warrants the most effective regulation," Baker said.

Currently, the Department of Housing and Urban Development and the Office of Federal Housing Enterprise Oversight regulate Freddie Mac and Fannie Mae. The Federal Housing Finance Board oversees the home loan bank system.
